- about: input_status_layout
  text: 'INPUT_STATUS (offset 12) reads switches in bits 7:0, then btn_up in bit 8, btn_down in bit 9 and btn_center in bit

- about: brightness_readback
  text: 'BRIGHTNESS always reads the stored value, never the switches. The display shows the effective brightness (the switches
    when CONTROL bit 0 is set), and the PWM changes with it on the next comparison, since the selection is combinational.'
- about: design_id
  text: 'DESIGN_ID reads 0x54314443 (ASCII T1DC) from the top level, and the same value is passed to fpga_shell; the shell
    build stamp is set to zero.'
- about: fpga_shell_source
  text: 'fpga_shell is instantiated but its source is not among the files of this run. The UART framing (assumed 8-N-1),
    the 100000-clock frame timeout, uart_rxd synchronization and the register protocol come from it and were not reviewed
    here.'
- about: assumption_buttons

  text: 'the interview answer asked for 2^17 (131072) clk cycles per digit, but spec.yaml, ARCHITECTURE.md and the RTL use DISPLAY_DIGIT_CYCLES = 100000. The RTL scans at 100000 cycles per digit; the spec disagrees with itself.'
- about: press_count_width
  text: 'an interview answer asked for 8-bit press counts wrapping at 256, but spec.yaml and the RTL use 32-bit counts (up_count, down_count, center_count) wrapping modulo 2^32. The RTL is what was built.'
- about: reset_style
  text: 'spec.yaml says asynchronous assertion with synchronized deassertion for all design state. In the RTL only the shell reset (shell_rst, from the two-flop reset_sync) has that style. The counter, registers, debouncers, PWM and display scan use a synchronous reset on rst = ~cpu_resetn, which is not synchronized, so releasing the button near a clk edge is unprotected for that logic. Constraints mark cpu_resetn as a false path, so timing analysis does not check it.'
- about: io_timing_constraints
  text: 'design.xdc sets input and output delays but then declares false paths from every input and to every output, so static timing analysis does not check the board I/O paths.'
- about: reset_values
  text: 'after reset: COUNTER 0, BRIGHTNESS 255 (0xFF), CONTROL 0 (switch brightness off, display enabled), all three press counts 0, win_rdata 0. DESIGN_ID always reads 1412514883 (0x54314443, ASCII T1DC).'
- about: unmapped_registers
  text: 'a read of any offset other than 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 or 28 returns 0. A write to an unmapped offset or to a read-only register (INPUT_STATUS, the press counts, DESIGN_ID) changes no register.'
- about: write_blocks_buttons
  text: 'in the RTL any write strobe (win_wr), even to an unmapped or read-only offset, takes the priority branch and suppresses the button update of COUNTER in that cycle. Press counts still increment. A write to COUNTER wins over buttons as spec.yaml says; a write to another address also costs a coincident button step.'
- about: button_priority
  text: 'when several buttons qualify in the same cycle, COUNTER follows centre first, then up, then down; the losing buttons still increment their own press counts. Presses are counted when the press is accepted (after DEBOUNCE_CYCLES stable cycles), not on release, and the counter changes in that same cycle.'
- about: input_status_raw
  text: 'INPUT_STATUS reads bits 7:0 as the switches, bit 8 as btn_up, bit 9 as btn_down and bit 10 as btn_center, taken directly from the top-level pins: they are neither synchronized nor debounced. Upper bits read 0.'
- about: partial_writes
  text: 'writes use the low bits only: COUNTER takes bits 15:0, BRIGHTNESS bits 7:0, CONTROL bits 1:0. Higher write-data bits are ignored. Reads are zero-extended to 32 bits.'
- about: read_latency
  text: 'win_rdata is a register loaded in the cycle win_rd is high, so read data is valid the cycle after the read strobe. It holds its value until the next read, and is cleared by reset.'
- about: brightness_display
  text: 'the seven-segment display and the LED PWM both use the effective brightness, so with CONTROL bit 0 set the two leftmost digits show the switch value, while BRIGHTNESS keeps its stored value. Digit AN[7] shows the high nibble and AN[6] the low nibble; AN[3:0] show the counter, AN[0] the lowest nibble.'
- about: fpga_shell_source
  text: 'the RTL instantiates fpga_shell with TIMEOUT_CYCLES 100000 and BUILD_STAMP 0, but the shell source is not in this run''s file list. UART framing and command syntax come from that module and were not reviewed here.'
- about: assumption_buttons
  text: 'assumption carried from the spec: BTNU, BTND and BTNC are active high; 8-N-1 framing and the nearest integer baud divider are assumed; the register map is byte-addressed with 32-bit alignment.'
